distinguishing_features: Adds a high-conductivity solid insert (Cu or Al2O3/W) at the ceramic-metal junction as a structural design change, not a software/telemetry inference or a duty-cycle setpoint change
Reduces local ΔT gradient across the junction via lateral heat spreading, lowering Δα·ΔT_local stress rather than derating temperature or cyclically shocking a deposit
Physically decouples CTE expansion vectors at the seal via a bonded interphase layer
Validated by AE crack-initiation and strain-gauge hysteresis on matched specimens
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce local thermal-stress concentration at a ceramic-metal bonded junction that arises from differential thermal expansion under repeated thermal cycling, so that crack initiation in the brittle ceramic is prevented.
parsed.viable_reason: A high-conductivity interphase insert is a physically sound, standard-manufacturable approach that plausibly lowers junction ΔT and is directly testable by AE/strain with a defined falsification criterion.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art uses a solid heat-spreading interphase to geometrically equalize the junction temperature field; the prior art instead relies on telemetry inference or duty-cycle derating, so arriving at a bonded conductive insert is not a routine application of the closest art.
